title: AI Researcher — Inference Optimization
description:
Role Overview
We are seeking an AI Researcher with deep experience in inference optimization to design, evaluate, and deploy high-performance inference systems for large-scale machine learning models. You will work at the intersection of model architecture, systems engineering, and hardware-aware optimization , improving latency, throughput, and cost efficiency across real-world production environments.
Key Responsibilities

• Research and develop techniques to optimize inference performance for large neural networks.

• Improve latency, throughput, memory efficiency, and cost per inference .

• Design and evaluate model-level optimizations (quantization, pruning, KV-cache optimization, architecture-aware simplifications).

• Implement systems-level optimizations (dynamic batching, kernel fusion, multi-GPU inference, prefill vs decode optimization).

• Benchmark inference workloads across hardware accelerators.

• Collaborate with engineering teams to deploy optimized inference pipelines .

• Translate research insights into production-ready improvements .

Required Qualifications

• Strong background in machine learning, deep learning, or AI systems .

• Hands-on experience optimizing inference for large-scale models .

• Proficiency in Python and modern ML frameworks (e.g., PyTorch).

• Experience with inference tooling (e.g., Triton, TensorRT, vLLM, ONNX Runtime).

• Ability to design experiments and communicate results clearly.

Preferred / Nice-to-Have Qualifications

• Experience deploying production inference systems at scale .

• Familiarity with distributed and multi-GPU inference .

• Experience contributing to open-source ML or inference frameworks .

• Authorship or co-authorship of peer-reviewed research papers in machine learning, systems, or related fields.

• Experience working close to hardware (CUDA, ROCm, profiling tools).

What Success Looks Like

• Measurable gains in latency, throughput, and cost efficiency .

• Optimized inference systems running reliably in production.

• Research ideas successfully translated into deployable systems.

• Clear benchmarks and documentation that inform product decisions.

Relevant Research Areas (Bonus)

• Long-context inference optimization

• Speculative decoding

• KV-cache compression and paging

• Efficient decoding strategies

• Hardware-aware inference design

title: U.S. Tax Compliance Manager
description:
Role Overview
We are seeking an experienced US Tax Compliance Manager to join our growing firm. This role is designed for a technically strong U.S. tax professional with 5-8 years of public accounting experience and significant experience preparing and reviewing U.S. federal and state tax filings.
The US Tax Compliance Manager will be responsible for overseeing the timely and accurate completion of U.S. tax compliance engagements for individuals, corporations, partnerships, trusts and estates. The role will provide technical review and guidance to the tax team, research complex compliance matters, monitor changes in U.S. tax legislation and help ensure consistent, high-quality delivery across the U.S. tax practice.
Canadian tax knowledge is considered an asset, but is not required. The primary focus of this position is U.S. tax compliance and technical expertise.

title: Mapping and Analysis of Family Language in African Union Agreed Language and Hum
description:
1. Background
Fòs Feminista . Fòs Feminista is an International Alliance of more than 200 partners across 40 countries working on the sexual and reproductive health, rights, and justice (SRHRJ) of women, girls, and gender-diverse people. In 2026, Fòs Feminista completed a three-decade mapping of how "family" has been used in United Nations agreed language - reviewing 1,441 excerpts across 180 UN documents from 1994 to 2025. That mapping found that a substantial, underused body of UN agreed language already centers individual rights, gender equality, and diverse family forms, offering feminist advocates a propositional foundation to build on rather than only a defensive posture against anti-rights mobilization around "family."
This mapping has not yet been extended to the regional level. The African Union (AU) has its own distinct body of human rights instruments, agreed language, and political dynamics relevant to family, gender equality, and SRHR - including the Protocol to the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights on the Rights of Women in Africa (the Maputo Protocol), one of the most progressive regional instruments globally on women’s rights, alongside AU mechanisms with an active record on ending child marriage and other harmful practices. At the same time, the AU is not insulated from anti-rights and anti-gender actors seeking to co-opt family language in multilateral outcomes.
As such, Fòs Feminista is seeking a consultant to conduct a systematic mapping and analysis of family-related language across African Union agreed language and human rights mechanisms to produce a rigorous, regionally grounded evidence base for use in African Union-level advocacy.
2. Purpose and Objectives
The purpose of this consultancy is to produce a systematic, evidence-based mapping of how "family" is defined, referenced, and used across African Union agreed language, in order to:

• Identify where existing AU agreed language already reflects rights-based, gender-equal, and diverse understandings of family, distinguishing this from areas where family language is used restrictively or left unaddressed.

• Produce a citable evidence base to inform feminist advocacy in African Union-level negotiations.

• Identify patterns specific to the African regional context - including but not limited to child marriage, female genital mutilation and other harmful practices, inheritance and marital property rights, and care - grounded in the region’s own instruments and mechanisms.

• Analyze whether language has changed over time, assessing whether it reflects advancement, regression, or stagnation in relation to gender equality and SRHR, and identifying the instruments, sessions or political context associated with such shifts.

• Generate concrete recommendations and draft rights-based language proposals for use in AU Summit declarations, Specialized Technical Committee outcomes, and other AU negotiating processes.

3. Scope of Work
The consultant will review family-related language across the following African Union instruments and mechanisms, at minimum:

• The African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights (1981) and its jurisprudence.

• The Protocol to the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights on the Rights of Women in Africa (Maputo Protocol, 2003), with particular attention to its marriage, family, and inheritance provisions.

• The African Charter on the Rights and Welfare of the Child (1990).

• Decisions, declarations, and resolutions of the AU Assembly of Heads of State and Government and the Executive Council.

• Resolutions, General Comments, and Concluding Observations of the African Commission on Human and Peoples’ Rights (ACHPR).

• General Comments and Concluding Observations of the African Committee of Experts on the Rights and Welfare of the Child (ACERWC).

As agents take on more of the software lifecycle, the hard part is no longer writing code - agents generate it faster than humans can review it, so the bottleneck shifts to verification and trust. We call that environment the harness (Agent = Model + Harness), and we're building a dedicated Harness Engineering team to own it. • Help design, build, and evolve the harness, the guides, feedback loops, guardrails, and shared context that turn raw model capability into production-grade engineering. This is a hands-on role; you will contribute to the development, not just direct it.

• Build and maintain feedforward guides (agent instruction files, reusable skills, architectural rules, reference docs, and codemods) that help agents get it right the first time and drive their adoption across teams.

• Build feedback sensors, custom linters, structural and architecture-fitness tests, verification loops, and LLM-as-judge reviewers - that catch issues automatically before they reach human reviewers.
